senses.sense_definition: A shield or shield-shaped surface on which a coat of arms is depicted; by extension, the coat of arms itself.

examples.text: The family <w>escutcheon</w> was carved in stone above the grand entrance of the manor.
Any dishonest act by an officer was considered a blot on the regiment's <w>escutcheon</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A decorative or protective metal plate or flange covering the gap around a pipe, valve, lock, or switch.

examples.text: The plumber slid a chrome <w>escutcheon</w> over the pipe to hide the opening in the wall.
He polished the brass <w>escutcheon</w> surrounding the keyhole on the antique cabinet.

senses.sense_definition: The decorative metal plate surrounding a keyhole or doorknob on a door.

examples.text: A decorative brass <w>escutcheon</w> framed the keyhole of the heavy oak door.
Before painting the exterior door, she carefully removed the metal <w>escutcheon</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A small shield placed in the center of a larger shield in heraldry.

examples.text: The heraldic artist painted a smaller <w>escutcheon</w> directly over the center of the main shield.
An <w>escutcheon</w> of pretence was added to show his wife's family lineage.

senses.sense_definition: The flat part of a ship's stern where the vessel's name is displayed.

examples.text: The ship's name was painted in gleaming gold lettering across the carved stern <w>escutcheon</w>.
Salt spray had weathered the wooden <w>escutcheon</w> on the old galleon's stern.

senses.sense_definition: The natural pattern and distribution of hair on the pubic mound.

examples.text: The physician noted the patient had a typically female pubic <w>escutcheon</w> during the examination.
Hormonal imbalances can noticeably alter the shape and density of the adult <w>escutcheon</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A pattern formed by hairs growing upward on the back of a cow's udder, historically used to judge milking capacity.

examples.text: Nineteenth-century dairy farmers closely inspected the cow's <w>escutcheon</w> to assess its value.
The width of the <w>escutcheon</w> was once believed to predict high milk production in dairy cattle.

senses.sense_definition: A depression or flattened area situated behind the beak in certain bivalve shells.

examples.text: The biologist identified the clam species by measuring the distinct <w>escutcheon</w> along the hinge line.
A smooth <w>escutcheon</w> extended behind the beak on each valve of the fossilized shell.
